speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that your psychiatric symptoms have improved, which is great news. Could you please describe the specific involuntary movements you are experiencing now, and where in your body do they occur?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of pneumonia seems incorrect for these specific neurological symptoms. Given your recent start on risperidone, I suspect this is akathisia, a common side effect characterized by inner restlessness. To confirm this and rule out other movement disorders, have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or involuntary facial grimacing along with this restlessness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of other neurological symptoms and your recent initiation of risperidone strongly supports a diagnosis of akathisia, a common extrapyramidal side effect. To confirm this clinical assessment and rule out other causes, I will order a neurological examination. REQUEST TEST: Neurological_Exam

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mental Status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Improved psychotic symptoms. Cranial Nerves: Intact. Motor: Normal tone and strength in all extremities. speaker: Doctor
text: The neurological exam confirms normal motor function but highlights your inability to sit still, which is classic for akathisia. This condition is a known side effect of risperidone and explains your restlessness and pacing. I recommend we adjust your medication or add a beta-blocker to manage this side effect. DIAGNOSIS READY: Akathisia
